models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light easterlies, flat sea - Panarea to Filicudi is a motor-sail; leave 06:00 for the 28 nm.
briefing.synopsis: A slack, low-gradient pattern sits over the Aeolians - nothing in the payload shows an organised system, just 3-9 kt of mostly E to SE breeze across the group. ECMWF IFS and AIFS (both 06Z 06 Oct) and ICON-2i (12Z 06 Oct) agree on a brief SSE freshening overnight, backing to S around dawn and returning E/ESE through tomorrow midday. Seas stay small throughout: 0.1-1.0 ft total wave and swell under 0.8 ft at every island through 08 Oct. Looking further out, the Salina-Portorosa leg on 09 Oct is the first day with thunderstorms in the picture.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Panarea, San Pietro buoy field is the pick and is rated sheltered (score 0.81) - though with SSE 8 kt it is on the exposed side of the headland, the alternatives at Drautto and Cala Zimmari score the same within noise, so the choice does not matter tonight. Expect SSE 8 kt with swell 0.7 ft from the ESE; consensus for 00:00 at Panarea shows 8.2 kt with gusts to 21.6 kt (ECMWF IFS gust field, 06Z run - an interval maximum, so it will feel less than that number suggests). The only thing that would move the fleet is if that SSE sets up a persistent roll into San Pietro, in which case Cala Zimmari gives a slightly different exposure arc.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Wind backs S to SSE by 06:00 and eases - Panarea shows 4.6 kt at that hour, but models disagree by more than 6 kt there (range 0.8-7.4 kt), so treat the early breeze as unreliable. Recommended departure is 06:00 for the 28 nm to Filicudi, arriving about 10:00 on a beam reach at 6 kt true, waves 0.8 ft. Later starts work too - no deterioration is flagged all day - but the wind goes aft and dies to a run by midday, so an early departure keeps the apparent wind usable; plan on engine time either way.

passage_notes.note: Go at all windows. Best is 06:00-10:00: SSE 6 kt, gusts 14 kt, 0.8 ft seas, beam reach. From 10:00 the wind goes E and it becomes a dead run at 5-6 kt - gusts to 16 kt are single-model interval maxima in light air, not squalls.

Very light - 3-5 kt all day, seas 0.5-0.7 ft. Morning S breeze gives a beam reach; from midday it goes ESE and dead on the nose, so leave early or motor. Reported gusts to 19 kt are interval maxima against a 5 kt mean.

Thunderstorms are forecast in most windows. Only the 10:00-14:00 slot scores go (N 5 kt, 1.5 ft); the payload flags deterioration after 11:00 and recommends a 09:00 departure. Re-brief this one on the day.

cautions: Panarea overnight gust of 21.6 kt (ECMWF IFS, 06Z run) against an 8 kt mean - an interval maximum, but worth a snubber check and a look at the buoy pennant before turning in.
Thunderstorms are in the 09 Oct Salina-Portorosa windows; the payload gives no storm timing detail beyond the window verdicts, so that leg needs a fresh look closer in.
Model spread exceeds 6 kt at several island points on 07 Oct (Panarea 06:00, 0.8-7.4 kt; Salina 12:00, 3.0-10.3 kt) - the mean is not a firm number.
The Portorosa berth entry for 10 Oct lists wind 13.8 kt with gust 10.5 kt, which is internally inconsistent; do not plan off that figure.
briefing.confidence_note: Run-to-run stability is tight at short range (mean wind shift 0.9 kt at 12-24 h, 1.3 kt at 24-48 h) and IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i agree on the light pattern, but direction shifts average 24° at two days and several points show 6+ kt spread, which matters a lot when the mean is only 5 kt.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
